question: Should authored-change scalability come from continued local optimization or a redesign of persistence and current-state reconstruction?
method: best-api-review/history-v2; redesign-from-first-principles; Best API target/scale gates; Plite ownership; existing Benchmark evidence
trigger: User asks whether to redesign or keep optimizing to become superior and scalable after the 10000-change reload comparison with ProseMirror.
requirements: Assess redesign versus further optimization for full ready-to-edit loading, scalable editing and retained history; do not claim universal superiority from a narrower ProseMirror workload.
Preserve native editable accepted/proposed/markup views, canonical document changes, atomic review, author identities, dependency/conflict semantics, named roots and selected historical compensation.
Preserve durable origin/offset anchors, retained deletions and required closed causal facts across reload, compaction, local undo and delayed collaboration; expire unavailable history explicitly.
Untrusted checkpoints must receive complete relevant structural and causal validation before publication; no trust flag, background replay or first-input delay may hide load cost.
Consider keep/configure, changed checkpoint API, new primitive, deleting replay, moving history lifetime, retained-content replacement and whole-substrate replacement before the verdict.

This is a bounded value review. Record one next design owner and the scale gate without implementing product changes, choosing an unmeasured runtime representation or opening another optimization trial.
evidenceReuse: Reconsidered the 2026-09-10 authored research and adoption records. The current adoption plan reports complete, superseding the compiled page’s stale S1–S3 wording. Reused the two reload benchmark plans and exact retained packets: all 193 loaded Plite source hashes in comparison-after.mjs.sources.json still match during this review. Freshly inspected stateCodec, restoreProjection, compaction, saved-range admission, collaboration snapshots, existing shared-effect checkpointing, raw example, Discussion decisions and AI cancellation. The bounded read-only reload_owner worker challenged checkpoint/history cuts; no independent model-family review, new benchmark or product test was run.
summary: Pursue redesigning authored persistence so current review state loads without full operation reduction and pending-edit replay. Keep native authored semantics and measured bulk wins. One directly validated live checkpoint plus a causal frontier and bounded suffix is the candidate family; compact live-state versus retained-content representation remains provisional pending Best API and its embedded Benchmark gate.
alternatives: Keep/configure: bulk decode and snapshot optimization remain the strongest smaller comparator and measured wins stay. They do not eliminate dependence on reconstructing current state from every stored operation.

Change existing API/format: use the native authored and existing codec/effect owners for directly loadable live records, pending content, durable positions and a causal frontier; preserve ordinary initialValue/value persistence unless a real history-retention job requires a new public contract.

Add primitive: reject a generic loader, trust flag, background replay controller or app-managed snapshot cache. They relocate work or add coordination without establishing coherent ready-to-edit state.

Delete/merge/move: remove full operation replay as the authority for current state; separate historical payload lifetime from live review facts. Do not delete origin identity, pending dependencies, collision facts, property precedence or compensation facts still required by current consumers.

Replace architecture: compare a compact live checkpoint against an identity-bearing retained-content representation that derives views without executing the historical edit sequence. This can remove more mapping work but is not selected or measured.

Plain marks/ranges: reject as a complete replacement for native authored state because inserted/deleted structure, causal dependencies, stable anchors and selective compensation are current jobs. Reintroducing those semantics recreates authored state.

Replace whole substrate or mandate a CRDT: not selected; no matched evidence shows that this removes more permanent complexity while retaining native/schema/review laws. Transport checkpointing already exists, while its authored payload still contains all operations.
proofLimits: Pursue authorizes further design only. Neither a direct live checkpoint nor a retained-content replacement was prototyped, benchmarked or accepted in this review. The current headless matched repair proves Bun 6.22s to 2.54s and Node 7.24s to 2.44s for 10055 pending insertion operations; 337 authored/Yjs tests, types and lint belong to that existing implementation. ProseMirror marks (16.6/31.8ms) lack equivalent causal history; plain document comparison is separate. All-pending load is not fixed merely by archiving closed history. Complete-load, first-edit, decisions, save, memory, malformed checkpoint, dependency/conflict, stable-anchor and delayed-peer proof must gate the selected representation. No browser/native, general scalability, all-feature API audit, new performance gain or publication claim is made. Earlier failed convergence research and prior receive-budget/build limits remain in their original artifacts.
